With this information Bank Julius Baer Europe S.A. (the “Bank”,
“we”, “our”) meet the requirements of section 15 (2) of the Luxem­
bourg Law of 8 March 2023 on the accessibility for products and
services, as amended (the “Accessibility Act”). This law is trans­
posing Directive (EU) 2019/882 of the European Parliament and
of the Council of 17 April 2019 on the accessibility requirements
for products and services into Luxembourg law. The Accessibility
Act aims to ensure accessibility of products and services offered
by companies. This means that companies must enable all con­
sumers to access the products and services offered. The goal is to
ensure that all consumers can equally participate in society.
Please note: This information is intended to explain our invest­
ment advice service in a clear manner. It is not legally binding. On­
ly your contract documents are legally binding.
This information is divided into four parts:
Part 1 contains specific information.
Here we explain investment advice and our services in con­
nection with investment advice.
Parts 2, 3 and 4 contain general information.

EXPLANATION OF OUR SERVICES
In this section, we explain investment advice and our associated
services. We will inform you about the main features and how in­
vestment advice works.
1.1

What is investment advice?
In our investment advice, we give you recommendations on finan­
cial instruments.
The following options are available:
–
Buy: We recommend that you buy a financial instrument.
–
Sale: We recommend that you sell a financial instrument.
–
Hold: We recommend that you do not sell a financial instru­
ment (but continue to hold it).
–
Do not buy: We recommend that you do not buy a financial
instrument.
As part of our investment advice, we take your financial situation
and your personal ideas into account. You will receive a declaration
of suitability from us with every consultation. This is a document in
which we explain how our recommendation suits you. In the end, you
decide for yourself whether you want to follow our recommendation.
Please note: Our recommendation is only valid at the time of the
consultation. We will only review the recommendation later if we
have agreed this with you in advance. If you have purchased finan­
cial instruments, you must therefore monitor their performance
yourself.
1.2

What are financial instruments?
The term “financial instruments” is used in laws relating to banks.
For example, it appears in the Luxembourg Law of 5 April 1993 on
the financial sector. Financial instruments i.a. include:
–
Securities, for example shares, bonds, certificates
and warrants,
–
Shares in investment funds
–

Derivatives
1.3

source.section: What is the investment advice process?

chunks.text:
What is the investment advice process?
Investment advice usually comprises four steps:
1.
Agreement: Before the Bank is able to provide you invest­
ment advice, you need to agree an Advisory Contract with us.
2.
Collection of information: We need certain information
from you in order to provide you with investment advice. We
ask you for certain personal data and your wishes regarding the
investment of your assets. This is required by law: We are not
allowed to advise you without your details. The information you
provide helps us to understand your interests and needs.
We need the following information from you:
–
Financial situation (What is your income? What are
your expenses? What are your assets?)
–
Loss-bearing capacity (What financial losses could you

bear?)
–
Investment goals (What do you want to achieve by
investing your assets? For example: long-term wealth

creation)
–
Investment horizon (For what period do you want to
invest your money?)
–

source.section: Risk appetite (What financial risks do you want to take?

chunks.text:
Risk appetite (What financial risks do you want to take?
For example: fluctuations in value, losses)
–
Sustainability preferences (Should sustainability crite­

chunks.text:
ria be taken into account when investing your assets?
For example: investments that contribute to achieving
an environmental goal)
–
Experience and knowledge in investing assets in finan­
cial instruments / Experience and knowledge in servic­
es related to financial instruments
3.
Recommendation: Based on your information, we will give
you recommendations on financial instruments. However,
we will only give you a recommendation if it matches your
information.
We will provide you with information about the recommend­
ed financial instruments, either verbally or through informa­
tion sheets. Examples of information sheets are the product
information sheet for shares and bonds or key information
sheets for investment funds.
4.
Documentation: In the final step, you will receive a written
summary of our recommendation, the suitability statement.
This summary includes our recommendation and an expla­
nation of how it suits you.
In the end, it is up to you to decide whether you want to follow our
recommendation.
In addition, before you buy or sell a financial product, we need
to make sure you are able to understand the nature and risks as­

It is at your discretion to refrain from making the trade or to pro­

source.section: 1.4 What costs do you incur for investment advice?

chunks.text:
1.4 What costs do you incur for investment advice?
For investment advice you pay us fees which are outlined in the
Schedule of Prices and Services of the Bank. Moreover, you will
usually receive cost information from us. This contains an over­
view of the costs and follow-up costs associated with buying, hold­
ing and selling a financial instrument. The cost information may
also contain information that we receive a payment from third par­
ties in connection with the purchase of a financial instrument. This
may, for example, be a payment from a fund company.
1.5

Is there a contract term?
The Advisory Agreement is concluded for an indefinite period of
time. It can be terminated from you and the Bank at any time with­
out the need provide any reasons.
You furthermore conclude the deposit agreement with us for an
indefinite period. You can terminate the deposit agreement at any
time without providing any reasons with a notice period of one
month. Further information can be gathered in the Bank’s General
Business Conditions.

source.section: 1.6 Is there a right to withdrawal?

chunks.text:
1.6 Is there a right to withdrawal?
You can revoke the Advisory Agreement within 14 days. However,
this only applies if the contract was concluded as a distance sell­
ing transaction, for example via the Internet or telephone, or as an
out-of-home transaction. In this case, you will receive certain le­
gal information from us. The cancellation period begins after you
have concluded the contract and have received all legal informa­
tion on it.
Please note: There is no right of cancellation when buying or sell­
ing financial instruments.

YOUR OPTIONS FOR PROVIDING FEEDBACK

OR FILING A COMPLAINT
We would be pleased to receive your feedback. Please address
your feedback directly to your relationship manager, he is glad to
be at your disposal. He is your direct contact person especially in
case of further enquiries concerning advisory services, portfolio
performance, transactions, banking services, pricing schedule,
IT-systems etc. Many things can be solved non-bureaucratic and
satisfying that way. Alternatively, if you have a complaint, please
address it in written form to us by using one of the following com­
munication channels:
Bank Julius Baer Europe S.A.

Attn. Complaint Management
14, rue Edward Steichen,

L-2540 Luxembourg
E-Mail: ComplaintManagement.Lux@juliusbaer.com
Furthermore, it is your discretion to address your complaint di­
rectly for the attention of our management board. In any case,
please take care to communicate the following information to­
gether with your complaint:
–
The reason for your complaint or a description of the identi­
fied mistake respectively
–
Your contact data (name and address as well as your account

number)
We will confirm the receipt of your written complaint within a max­
imum of 10 business days and we will take care of an answer as
fast as possible, but not later than one month. If in particular cases
it takes us more than one month to respond, we will inform you
about this. If your complaint is relating to payment services, the
Bank will provide feedback within 15 days.
If you are not satisfied with our response, you may refer your com­
plaint directly to the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Fi­
nancier (CSSF):
The CSSF is competent to receive complaints from customers
(natural or legal persons) of the professionals subject to its super­
vision and to act as an intermediary in order to seek an amicable
settlement of these complaints. The CSSF acts in its capacity as
alternative dispute resolution (“ADR”) entity, notably pursuant to
the European legislation relating to the out-of-court resolution of
consumer disputes that was transposed into Luxembourg law and
introduced into the Consumer Code in 2016. The CSSF is regis­
tered on the list of ADR entities within the meaning of Article L.
431-1 of the Consumer Code and on the list of ADR entities es­

tablished and published by the European Commission. The com­
plaints that are sent to the CSSF are handled by its legal depart­
ment: “Legal Department Consumer Protection/Financial Crime”
of the CSSF. The out-of-court resolution of disputes takes place
on a voluntary basis and is free of charge. In order to facilitate the
filing of a complaint, the CSSF publishes a complaint form on its
website: https://www.cssf.lu/en/customer-complaints/. The com­
plaint form can either be filed online or sent by mail, fax or email:

CHARACTERISTICS OF ACCESSIBILITY

OF OUR SERVICES
You would like to know how we meet the requirements of the Ac­
cessibility Act with regard to our services? In this section, we will
inform you about the characteristics of the accessibility of our ser­
vices.
Background:
The Accessibility Act obliges us, among other things, to adhere
to guidelines for accessible web content. These guidelines are in­
tended to enable all people, especially those with disabilities, to
access web content. The guidelines are based on four principles
of accessibility:
–
Perceivability: As many people as possible should be able
to perceive information and IT functions. This means, that
we, for example, ensure that for each image or graphic there
is an alternative means of perception available, such as writ­
ten text.
–
Operability: As many people as possible should be able to
use the IT functions. This means, for example, that we en­
sure our web content can be operated using an ordinary key­
board.
–
Understandability: As many people as possible should be
able to read and understand the web content clearly. For ex­
ample, we offer our web content in simple and understand­
able language whenever possible
–

Robustness: The web content must be compatible with
so-called assistive technologies as far as possible. Assistive
technologies include, for example, programmes for reading
out or enlarging web content, but also for converting speech
into text. This means, for example, that we ensure important
standards for the use of assistive technologies are observed,
such as the technical structure and labelling of the content.
We meet the requirements of the Accessibility Act by implement­
ing these principles in our services.
3.1
Accessibility of services
The following describes the characteristics of the accessibility of
our services in combination with investment advice:
–
We can send you the Advisory Agreement by post or elec­
tronically as a PDF via email. Please contact your relation­
ship manager and request that it will be sent to you through
your preferred communication channel.

3.2 Accessibility of this information
The characteristics of accessibility of this information are as follows:
–
We provide you with this information through various access
channels, namely via a personal handover by your relation­
ship manager or via the Bank’s website (www.juliusbaer.com).
–
The content of this information is written in clear language.
The B2 level of the Common European Framework of Refer­
ence for languages (CEFR) is not exceeded.
Note: This does not apply to the actual service contract or the
General Business Conditions (GBC) and pre-contractual infor­
mation that are connected to the service contract.
–
The layout of this information has a specific design, and the
description of the typography used, e.g. the font, line length,
line spacing and highlighting of important texts were chosen
to be user-friendly.

3.3 Accessibility of documents related to our services
The characteristics of accessibility of documents related to our
services (including this information) are as follows:
Documents are perceivable. This means:
–
Documents have partly the format PDF-UA and/or are webbased. This format can be converted into other formats.
They can be enlarged for better readability. Screen-readers
can interpret the documents and read aloud the content on
the screen. Therefore, the documents are available to you
through several sensory channels.
4

COMPETENT MARKET SURVEILLANCE AUTHORITY
Do you have problems concerning the accessibility of our servic­
es? In this section we will inform you about who you can contact.
The competent authority in Luxembourg is called «Office de la
surveillance de l’accessibilité des produits et services » (OSAPS)
OSAPS will, among other things, act as a reference point for ac­
cessibility. OSAPS will provide companies with guidelines, tools
and advice to help them improve the accessibility of their products
and/or services. In addition, any person can inform OSAPS of the
non-compliance of a product or service.
If you have problems with our service, you can submit a complaint
to the OSAPS. The OSAPS may then initiate legal measures
against us. In your complaint, you can claim that we are violating
a requirement of the Accessibility Act The contact details of the
OSAPS are:
